summary:
FSD (Supervised) is still a $99-a-month subscription in the U.S.; Tesla no longer sells it outright [2][3]. Tesla counted 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions at the end of Q3 [4].

The software didn't change this week, but its package did: update 2026.44.1 went to wide release carrying FSD v14.3.13 on AI4 cars and v14.3 Lite on HW3 [41][42]. HW3 still won't get unsupervised FSD, and Tesla's target for unsupervised FSD in owners' cars is Q2 2027, inside Robotaxi zones first [5][6]. In Europe, the Dutch regulator approved an update that makes Tesla Assisted Driving require hands on the wheel above 130 km/h and attention during maneuvers; U.S. drivers face no such rule [43].

Robotaxi kept growing. Miami's zone nearly doubled to about 59 square miles [44], and Tesla hinted that Dallas Cybercab rides are close, without a date [45]. Cybercab orders opened by invitation at $29,990 plus a required $299-a-month subscription, with Texas deliveries targeted for December [46]. Musk said owners' cars "may start trials" on the network next month, with no details on who qualifies [47]. Tesla plans a €3 billion Cybercab factory in Berlin, though Europe has no approval for unsupervised driving [53].

Safety data drew attention. Electrek counts 8 Cybercab crashes in NHTSA files, the driverless ones all under 5 mph [49]. Tesla's own NHTSA reports say Autopilot or FSD was engaged in a fatal September Model X crash in Naples, Florida, and in a May crash on I-75 that killed three; the reports don't say which system or that it caused the crashes [50][51]. Meanwhile Tesla is running its first FSD billboard in Times Square, claiming FSD is "7x safer" than a human, a figure it doesn't independently back up [52].

price.purchase: Can't be bought outright: Tesla says FSD (Supervised) is subscription-only [2]. The $8,000 one-time purchase ended after February 14, 2026 [3].
price.note: FSD bought outright by an earlier owner stays with the car unless it was transferred away before March 31, 2026; a previous owner's subscription does not carry over, and Luxe Package FSD may carry over depending on when it was bought [2].

versions.note: 2026.44.1 began rolling out November 17 and went to wide release; it carries the same v14.3.13 that reached AI4 cars in October, plus Charger Network View and security fixes [41][42]. Rewritten AI compiler, vision-encoder upgrades and Automatic Collision Evasion [1][42]. In Europe, AI4 cars run Tesla Assisted Driving 14.2.2.x in 2026.39 builds [27][40]; an RDW-approved update adds earlier attention warnings, a strike for not watching during maneuvers and hands on the wheel above 130 km/h [43]. Tesla's manuals now call this computer SI4 [21].

Distilled from v14 for HW3: parking, unparking, reversing, Arrival Options and Speed Profiles, including a new SLOTH profile [1][19]. Now carried in 2026.44.1, which Tesla Oracle says reached roughly 80% of eligible HW3 cars in its wide release [41].

check: In the car: Controls > Software > Additional Vehicle Information shows the Autopilot computer (2.5, 3 or 4); this needs software 2024.38 or later [12].
Controls > Software also shows whether Full Self-Driving Capability is in the car's included package [2].
Front cameras: AI4 cars show two red lenses and one black dummy lens; AI4 side repeaters have a red tint [12].
Build date: S/X after about March 2023, U.S. Model Y after late May 2023 and the 2024 Model 3 are likely AI4 [12].
Tesla's owner's manuals now call the computer the "SI Computer": HW3 is listed as SI3 and AI4 as SI4. Same hardware, new name [21].
transfer: You can no longer move FSD to another car or account: Tesla's FSD (Supervised) Transfer Program ended on March 31, 2026 [2][3]. If you sell a car whose FSD was bought outright, the purchase stays with that car, so the next owner gets it [2]. If you had a subscription, it ends with your ownership and the buyer must subscribe on their own Tesla account [2]. There is no current transfer offer. The new referral program is not a transfer: subscribers get a free month and outright owners a $99 Tesla credit for each referral who subscribes, up to 12 a year, in app 4.62 or later [30].

robotaxi.status: No one on board; Cybercabs in the fleet [9][14]. On November 9 the zone grew from about 272 to 443 square miles [37]. NHTSA files list 8 Cybercab crashes, mostly in August and September; the four driverless ones were all under 5 mph [49]. Service customers in Austin are being offered Robotaxi rides instead of Uber credits or loaners [48]. Texas registrations top 1,500 robotaxis, over 700 of them Cybercabs, not all in service [45]
No one on board [14]; Tesla said Cybercab rides would start in Dallas in November and on November 18 hinted a launch is close, but none was confirmed [6][45]
No one on board [14]; on October 26 the zone grew from about 25 to an estimated 254 square miles, by third-party trackers' count [23]
Launched November 2 at 6 a.m.; the zone runs west of downtown to TCU and White Settlement and along I-820 toward Saginaw [28]; reported as unsupervised [33]

Unsupervised rides since July 3 [44]; on November 16 the zone nearly doubled, from about 31 to 59 square miles, adding downtown, Brickell, Wynwood, Little Havana and Hialeah; Miami Beach is still outside [44]

Launched November 9 at 5 a.m. with a 274-square-mile zone on paper from Loop 1604 to south of downtown; the airport is inside but not served. Whether rides carry a safety monitor wasn't reported at launch [35]
Safety driver required by California rules; not driverless [5][7]
Announced as coming soon; no dates [7][8]

buying: Check Controls > Software for Full Self-Driving Capability: only an outright purchase stays with the car [2].
Don't count on moving FSD from your old car; transfers ended March 31, 2026 [2].
Prefer AI4: HW3 gets the Lite build and won't run unsupervised FSD [1][5].
On a 2017-2019 S/X or early Model 3, confirm the computer is HW3 or later, not HW2/HW2.5 [12][13].
Budget $99 a month if the car has no purchased FSD [2].
Outside the U.S., don't buy a car with an aftermarket FSD unlock: Korean police booked 80 people for using such devices, which carry up to two years in prison there [26].
Selling a car with purchased FSD? It stays with the car, so price it in; a referral reward is not a way to move it [2][30].
A personal Cybercab ($29,990, invite-only) needs a $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription and delivers first in Texas Robotaxi areas, from December [46].
Plan on supervising: Musk says owners might trial adding cars to Robotaxi as soon as December, but nothing about eligibility or pay has been set [47].
changes: Update 2026.44.1 went to wide release with the same FSD: v14.3.13 on AI4, v14.3 Lite on HW3 [41][42].
Europe: an RDW-approved update makes Tesla Assisted Driving demand hands on the wheel above 130 km/h and attention during maneuvers [43].
Miami's Robotaxi zone nearly doubled to about 59 square miles on November 16, adding downtown and Brickell [44].
Cybercab orders opened by invitation at $29,990 plus $299 a month; deliveries targeted for December in Texas [46].
Musk said owners' cars 'may start trials' on the Robotaxi network next month; no details [47].
Austin service customers are being offered Robotaxi rides in place of loaners or Uber credits [48].
Tesla hinted at an imminent Dallas Cybercab launch; not yet confirmed [45].
Electrek counts 8 Cybercab crashes in NHTSA files, and Tesla reported Autopilot or FSD engaged in a fatal Model X crash in Naples on September 30 [49][50].
Tesla ran its first FSD billboard in Times Square, through the end of November [52].
Tesla plans a €3 billion Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin, with production from 2029 [53].

pt.summary:
O FSD (Supervised) continua sendo uma assinatura de US$ 99 por mês nos EUA; a Tesla não vende mais a compra definitiva [2][3]. A Tesla contou 1,74 milhão de assinaturas ativas do FSD no fim do 3º trimestre [4].

O software não mudou nesta semana, mas o pacote sim: a atualização 2026.44.1 foi liberada em larga escala com o FSD v14.3.13 nos carros AI4 e o v14.3 Lite no HW3 [41][42]. O HW3 continua sem previsão de FSD sem supervisão, e a meta da Tesla para o FSD sem supervisão nos carros de clientes é o 2º trimestre de 2027, primeiro dentro das zonas do Robotaxi [5][6]. Na Europa, o regulador holandês aprovou uma atualização que obriga o Tesla Assisted Driving a exigir mãos no volante acima de 130 km/h e atenção durante manobras; nos EUA não existe essa regra [43].

O Robotaxi continuou crescendo. A zona de Miami quase dobrou, para cerca de 59 milhas quadradas [44], e a Tesla deu a entender que as corridas de Cybercab em Dallas estão próximas, sem data [45]. As encomendas do Cybercab abriram por convite a US$ 29.990, mais uma assinatura obrigatória de US$ 299 por mês, com entregas no Texas previstas para dezembro [46]. Musk disse que carros de clientes "podem começar testes" na rede no mês que vem, sem detalhes sobre quem se qualifica [47]. A Tesla planeja uma fábrica de Cybercab de € 3 bilhões em Berlim, embora a Europa não tenha aprovado a direção sem supervisão [53].

Os dados de segurança chamaram atenção. A Electrek conta 8 acidentes do Cybercab nos registros da NHTSA, os sem motorista todos abaixo de 5 mph [49]. Os próprios relatórios da Tesla à NHTSA dizem que o Autopilot ou o FSD estava ativo num acidente fatal de um Model X em setembro em Naples, na Flórida, e num acidente em maio na I-75 que matou três pessoas; os relatórios não dizem qual sistema nem que ele causou os acidentes [50][51]. Enquanto isso, a Tesla exibe seu primeiro anúncio do FSD na Times Square, dizendo que o FSD é "7x mais seguro" que um humano, número que ela não comprova de forma independente [52].

de.summary:
FSD (Supervised) bleibt in den USA ein Abo für 99 Dollar im Monat; zum Festpreis verkauft Tesla es nicht mehr [2][3]. Ende des dritten Quartals zählte Tesla 1,74 Millionen aktive FSD-Abos [4].

Die Software blieb diese Woche gleich, das Paket nicht: Update 2026.44.1 ging in die breite Verteilung, mit FSD v14.3.13 auf AI4-Autos und v14.3 Lite auf HW3 [41][42]. HW3 bekommt weiterhin kein unbeaufsichtigtes FSD, und Teslas Ziel für unbeaufsichtigtes FSD in Kundenautos ist das zweite Quartal 2027, zuerst in den Robotaxi-Zonen [5][6]. In Europa hat die niederländische Zulassungsbehörde ein Update genehmigt, mit dem Tesla Assisted Driving über 130 km/h die Hände am Lenkrad und bei Manövern Aufmerksamkeit verlangt; in den USA gibt es diese Regel nicht [43].

Robotaxi wuchs weiter. Die Zone in Miami hat sich auf rund 59 Quadratmeilen fast verdoppelt [44], und Tesla deutete an, dass Cybercab-Fahrten in Dallas bald starten, ohne Datum [45]. Bestellungen für den Cybercab sind auf Einladung für 29.990 Dollar möglich, plus ein Pflichtabo von 299 Dollar im Monat; Auslieferungen in Texas sind für Dezember geplant [46]. Musk sagte, Kundenautos könnten nächsten Monat erste Tests im Netz beginnen, ohne Angaben dazu, wer teilnehmen darf [47]. Tesla plant in Berlin ein Cybercab-Werk für 3 Milliarden Euro, obwohl Europa unbeaufsichtigtes Fahren nicht zugelassen hat [53].

Die Sicherheitsdaten fanden Beachtung. Electrek zählt 8 Cybercab-Unfälle in den NHTSA-Daten, die fahrerlosen alle unter 5 mph [49]. Teslas eigene NHTSA-Meldungen geben an, dass Autopilot oder FSD bei einem tödlichen Model-X-Unfall im September in Naples, Florida, und bei einem Unfall im Mai auf der I-75 mit drei Toten aktiv war; welches System und ob es den Unfall verursacht hat, sagen die Meldungen nicht [50][51]. Derweil zeigt Tesla seine erste FSD-Werbung am Times Square und nennt FSD „7x sicherer“ als einen Menschen – eine Zahl, die nicht unabhängig belegt ist [52].
